title: Chrono-batched upgrade safety probes and rollback orchestration for VPC control plane
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Build a time-windowed, batch-based canary mechanism for Private (VPC) control plane upgrades that minimizes blast radius, automatically validates functional and SLO guardrails, and orchestrates deterministic rollbacks when probes fail. This ticket implements Terraform orchestration, a lightweight in-cluster probe runner, and an operator-side promotion/rollback controller integrated with our release pipeline and console workflows.
background: Current private control plane upgrades are mostly wave-based with manual health verification. Recent incidents surfaced cases where a faulty control-plane binary rolled through multiple sites before an operator manually intervened. We need a safer, automated version promotion model that 1) performs chronologically batched promotions by customer cohort/time-slice, 2) executes a fixed probe suite per cohort (smoke, KV cache warming, API latency SLOs), and 3) supports fast, deterministic rollback with post-mortem artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (modules/controlplane/upgrade_flow) that declares cohort groups, batch windows, and probe policies and can be applied without manual steps
An in-cluster probe-runner (containerized) that executes the canonical probe suite and emits structured pass/fail events to our control plane telemetry topic
Promotion controller that reads probe events and advances cohorts when all pass; rolls back cohorts automatically when any critical probe fails
End-to-end test harness that simulates failures and validates rollback path in CI without touching production VPCs
Runbook updated with clear operator actions and SLAs for auto-rollback scenarios
Security review completed for probe runner and Terraform IAM role changes
implementation_steps: Design Terraform schema to express cohorts, time-windows, and probe policy; add examples for small/medium/large customers
Add Terraform outputs and data sources to wire cohort membership to the operator via SSM parameter store / secret manager as appropriate
Develop probe-runner service: smoke tests (control-plane APIs), KV cache sanity checks, tail-latency calcs, and synthetic workload generator
Instrument probes to produce structured events to kafka/redwood-telemetry-prod (topic: controlplane-upgrade-probes) with trace IDs
Implement promotion controller in the operator that subscribes to telemetry, enforces quorum rules, and triggers kubernetes label-based promotions
Create CI-only test harness (k8s-in-docker) that can flip failure flags to validate rollback choreography
Author terraform docs and example job for customers using private control plane to opt into chrono-batched upgrades
testing_plan: Unit tests for Terraform schema validation and plan-time defaults
Integration tests: spin up two control plane replicas in a sandbox VPC, run probe-runner against canary, verify promotion on green, verify rollback on injected failure
Chaos tests: introduce network partition and sim latency to ensure probe-runner fails safely and triggers rollback
Load test: ensure probe-runner probe suite completes within configured time-window under 99th percentile service load
Security tests: IAM role least-privilege verification and container scanning
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Staging: Deploy Terraform module and operator change in staging, run full test harness (owners: Marco, Priya)
Phase 1 - Pilot cohort: Enable chrono-batched upgrades for 10 internal customer VPCs, monitor for 72 hours
Phase 2 - Expanded pilot: 100 customers spread across three regions, telemetry validation and slack alerts enabled
Phase 3 - Default opt-in: Flip console toggle to enable chrono-batched promotion for new private deployments, document opt-out path
Rollback policy: immediate rollback for any critical probe (API error, SLO breach > 2x threshold) or manual pause if ambiguous signals
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboards: grafana/dashboard-controlplane-upgrade-cohorts (new panel for active cohort state and recent probe results)
Alerts: pager on rollback_count > 0 for production cohorts; slack incident channel alerts for probe failures in pilot
Logging: structured probe events with trace_id and cohort_id; retention 90d for upgrade traces
runbook_and_playbooks: Runbook: steps to manually pause promotions, force rollback, and collect artifacts (logs, probe events, cluster snapshots)
Post-mortem checklist: timeline reconstruction using trace_ids and cohort membership, customer-impact mapping, mitigation latency analysis
Operator playbook: when auto-rollback occurs, validate root cause, confirm rollback integrity, and schedule remedial patch rollout
security_considerations: Probe-runner must run under dedicated service account with least privilege to query control-plane health endpoints only
Terraform changes require an approver from Security for IAM role additions and any cross-account data retrieval
All probe payloads must avoid sending PII to telemetry; use hashed/filtered identifiers
Ensure TLS mutual auth between probe-runner and control-plane endpoints in private deployments
